newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Edgars at 5-month low after poor results.
newsitem.headline: Edgars at 5-month low after poor results.

text.p: Shares in South African retailing group Edgars Ltd fell to their lowest levels in five months on Wednesday after posting year results well below analysts' expectations, dealer said.
"Their results were taken disastrously relative to the entire stores sector," a dealer on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said.
By 0900 GMT the share had lost 12 rand, or 10.91 percent, to 98 rand, bringing its losses to 15 percent since the beginning of the week. Volumes traded on Wednesday were worth over 4.7 million rand.
Shares last touched 98 rand in December 1996.

Edgars on Tuesday reported attributable earnings for the year to end-March down five percent at 320.9 million rand, which translated into earnings per share of 598.0 cents. Analysts polled by Reuters had expected earnings at a consensus 638 cents per share.
It declared a flat total dividend of 247 cents.
Edgars said business in the first six months of its new financial year would remain tight amid expected continued subdued economic activity.
Dealers said the share should start stabilising in between the 90 to 98 rand level.
